Fig1_Polynya_source_footprint: Antarctic polar stereographic map of the 85 matched Adélie sites, coloured by each site's mean observed June–October coastal-polynya area fraction within 100 km. A pale generalized Natural Earth 1:110m land outline and labelled 0, 90 west and 90 east meridians provide geographic context only; land is not used as an analysis mask. Thin blue outlines show 100-km geodesic sampling circles, not polynya boundaries. A region table totals 439 colony-seasons in 11 regions during 2004–2010. The geodesically calibrated scale bar is centred at 70 degrees south. All original colony locations and exposure values are unchanged.
Fig2_Polynya_association_and_sensitivity: Forest plot of four unchanged polynya coefficients for original and author-R1000 optical measurements, without and with summer salinity adjustment. Each row pairs a filled coloured CV3 delete-one-region jackknife interval with a hollow grey archived CR1 interval. Both use 425 informative rows, 82 sites, 8 regions and t(7). All four CV3 main-association intervals remain below zero. A separate plot shows all 11 leave-region-out point estimates for each original model; every point remains negative, without omission-specific intervals. Original eleven-region and archived eight-region numeric tables are preserved separately. Layout is 169 mm wide with visible text at least 10 pt.
Fig3_Preceding_following_winter_contrast: Time order of preceding winter P0, summer optical isotope proxy, and following winter P1 on 358 matched observations. Four paired forest rows show original P0, original P1, original P0 minus P1, and author-R1000 P0 minus P1. Filled coloured CV3 delete-one-region jackknife intervals are compared with hollow grey archived eight-region CR1 intervals, all with t(7) and 347 informative observations. The original contrast remains minus 0.68769 per mil per 10 percentage points; its CV3 interval is minus 1.47026 to plus 0.09487. The author-R1000 contrast CV3 interval is minus 1.47634 to plus 0.08980. Both CV3 contrast intervals cross zero, so the timing difference is uncertain despite the negative point estimates. Frozen eleven-region intervals remain in the numeric extract rather than the main panel. Layout is 169 mm wide with visible text at least 10 pt.
Fig4_Polynya_salinity_conditional_inform: Scatter plot of winter polynya and summer salinity residuals after site and region-by-season effects only, on the same 439 observations, with correlation minus 0.08043. A bar plot reports additional residual variation relative to M0: salinity 2.1429%, polynya 3.7939%, and both 5.2928%. These modest conditional associations do not identify independent physical causes.
Fig5_Observation_and_unresolved_pathways: Conceptual figure separating the observed negative historical within-colony association from three unresolved candidate pathways: trophic composition, nitrogen-isotope baseline, and optical mixture or surface effects. The observed association has no causal arrowhead; candidate pathways use dashed arrows. A distinct shaded panel places the Reaves et al. 2025 southern latent-heat-polynya settings and higher bone delta15N in southern colonies in a separate between-colony context: 15 locations with modern and ancient chick bones. The tissue, timescale and estimand differ; no continuous polynya-area slope, direct sign reversal or proven mechanism is implied.
